A deferred, resumable design plan for restyling a Vite + React + Tailwind demo (sign-in, sub-nav, guided tour, timeline activity, live totals, realtime sync) without losing context between sessions.
Every data change must leave an audit record that application code cannot forge, skip or edit, so a trigger writes the log and nobody can update or delete it.
Deciding whether a dashboard total or group-by is computed in browser JavaScript or in a Postgres view, defaulting to JavaScript until measurement says otherwise.
A multi-tenant API must answer 404, never 403, when a resource belongs to another tenant, so an attacker cannot confirm that it exists.
Drop the FK on `public.users.id → auth.users(id)`; integrity via triggers
Choosing what to show when a list is empty (an action button, a hint, or just a message) by asking whether the user can fix it right now, can not fix it, or is only viewing.
Keeping secrets out of source control and build-time settings apart from runtime settings by using three env files with separate purposes and never overlapping names.
Writing an algorithm in a spec as a numbered procedure plus a JavaScript fixture and self-test, so the algorithm can be tested instead of left as untestable prose.
The §0.0 cheapest-version line is missing
Writing SQL migrations and seeds that can be re-applied safely any number of times, using idempotency primitives on every statement.
Lets the kit grow from each consumer project: scaffold from the kit, record decisions in the consumer, then mine those decisions for new patterns and land them through the KITTING workflow.
Using a cheaper worker model that has no CLI or API by having a human relay a tight, task-shaped brief into its desktop app, while the auditor independently re-verifies the result.
Helps decide whether and why to enforce tenant isolation with PostgreSQL row-level security, and lists the questions to answer and the tests to have before adopting it.
Gives a multi-tenant app a runbook template, five must-have alerts and a liveness/readiness health split, so a 2am problem report has a five-minute path to a fix.
Stops slow or failing email sends and background jobs from breaking the user request, by writing an outbox or job row in the same transaction and letting a cron worker deliver it with retries.
Prevents works-on-my-machine drift and committed build artefacts by pinning exact dependency versions, gitignoring generated files, and keeping generated manifests in lockstep with their sources.
Makes a multi-table write atomic and race-safe when the user role cannot write every table, by putting the cascade in a SECURITY DEFINER Postgres function with FOR UPDATE and calling it through rpc.
Makes forgetting the tenant filter impossible in Prisma by injecting tenantId into every query through a $extends hook and an AsyncLocalStorage guard set once per request.
Produces a public-ready sibling copy of a private TINS workspace with methodology and LLM-authorship traces scanned out of the whole tree and fresh public documentation written.
Gives an app a minimum-viable offline experience without a write-queue: read the cached snapshot offline, disable mutations offline, using a hook, a banner and a form-level guard.
Avoids both hard errors and silent partial success when a request exceeds what is available, by recording what was possible and returning the gap as a first-class shortfall field.
Decides whether a third-party MCP server or agent skill is safe to recommend, by reading it against nine red flags and ending in SAFE, REVIEW-REQUIRED or UNSAFE, never by running it.

Decides which decisions an autonomous LLM may make alone and which it must park for a human, by reversibility and blast radius rather than difficulty, with uncertainty always resolving upward to the human.
Enforces multi-tenant isolation in Prisma by using two clients, a superuser one for cross-tenant work and an RLS-enforced one for tenant sessions, plus a helper that picks the right one.
Lets contributors propose spec changes as a separate merge-ready amendment file with the same section numbering, so the spec author can merge it in one sitting instead of resolving edit conflicts.
